Sandbox_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Inc: How many in-game hours wrapped milk takes to set at its best temperature (40 to 45°C). Cooler milk sets more slowly.
Sandbox_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Cul: How many in-game hours the Starter Culture Crock's first stage takes at the best temperature. The second stage, after the fresh milk, takes half as long.
Sandbox_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Tem: How much the temperature slows setting and the starter culture. Off makes them run at full speed in any weather (the milk still has to cool before the wrap goes on).
Sandbox_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Mil: Raw milk sours after about a day and a half in a 20°C room (3 to 4 days in a summer basement, a week in a winter one, 8 in a powered fridge, never frozen), then spoils as long again after. Milk scalded, held at 85°C for 20 minutes (a Stone Hearth's cauldron, a stove or a fire) never sours: it keeps as long and then spoils. Sealed store milk keeps until it is poured out.
1 is the times above. 2 goes off twice as fast, 0.5 keeps twice as long. On top of the game's own Food Spoilage setting: Very Slow milk keeps 2.5 times as long at 1 here.
Sandbox_TraditionalPreservationDairy_But: Butter goes rancid: about 30 days fresh in a 15°C cellar, 75 in a powered fridge, 20 in a 20°C room, 15 at 25°C and over, never frozen. Salted Butter keeps three times as long. Clarified Butter never goes off. Off, butter never spoils, as in the base game. On top of the game's own Food Spoilage setting.
Sandbox_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Fro: At 0°C and below, six hours of frost in all freeze a thing through: wet kefir grains go Hungry (one milk change brings them back), kefir separates into curds and whey, and a yogurt is Thawed, a little less pleasant to eat. An Active Yogurt Starter loses a little of its life each frozen hour: two days of frost spend it. Dried grains, milk and butter come to no harm, and what sets in the Culturing Pot or the crock only waits. A basement never freezes, nor a place by a lit fire or banked embers. Off, the cold does no harm.
